newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: TRIPLE P SEES LOSS IN THIRD QUARTER.
newsitem.headline: TRIPLE P SEES LOSS IN THIRD QUARTER.

text.p: Dutch software group Triple P NV said on Friday it expected a provisional operating loss of 7.5 million guilders on revenues of 77 million in the third quarter of 1996.
It added it would take an additional 16.5 million guilder one-off restructuring charge in this quarter but expected to return to profit in the final quarter.
In the third quarter of 1995 the Nasdaq-listed company posted a positive operating income of 4.2 million guilders on net revenues of 81.8 million.

The restructuring programme included a reduction of its workforce in the Netherlands, Germany, Belgium and France by 225 people. "The majority of this reduction will be realized by attrition, early retirement and through the divestiture of five non-strategic business units," Triple P said in a statement.
It said it had already spun off three non-core businesses, which represented expected 1996 revenues of about 12 million guilders and operating losses of 3.5 million.
In this year and in 1997, two more units will be sold with an expected 1996 turnover of eight million guilders and break-even results.

A further two units will not be sold but restructured. These are expected to post 1996 joint turnover of 13 million guilders and restructuring them is expected to result in savings of three million guilders a year.
The total restructuring programme for the group is expected to improve annual operating income by about 23 million guilders a year, it said.
As part of the divestment programme, Dutch publisher Wolters Kluwer bought the intellectual property rights of Triple P's accountancy software unit in the Netherlands.
It also sold its unit Labinfo Systems to Delaware Computing BV, a subsidiary of Belgium's Bekaert Group .
No financial details of these transactions were given.
Triple P said it would publish full third quarter figures in early November.
